marks.gloss_en: ואמר רבי יוחנן: שכל מקום שהלך שם ביתו עמו -- Shmuel carried his household with him and so took nothing from anyone
one who wishes to benefit [from others' hospitality] may benefit, like Elisha
תניא נמי הכי: לא יעמוד אדם לא על גבי כסא ולא על גבי שרפרף ולא במקום גבוה ויתפלל, אלא במקום נמוך ויתפלל
the baraita: one should stand neither on a chair, nor on a stool, nor in a high place and pray, but in a low place and pray
בשלמא למאן דאמר אכסדרה, היינו דכתיב קיר; אלא למאן דאמר עלייה, מאי קיר? -- an upper storey has no 'wall' to speak of
שקירוה -- kir is kirui: they roofed it (= p_kir_kerui, held aliba the upper-storey view)
on the upper-storey view, 'kir' means they roofed it (kirui), not 'wall'
בשלמא למאן דאמר עלייה, היינו דכתיב עליית; אלא למאן דאמר אכסדרה, מאי עליית? -- a divided veranda is no 'upper storey'
מעולה שבבתים -- aliyat means the most excellent of the rooms (= p_aliyat_meula, held aliba the veranda view)
on the veranda view, 'aliyat' means the most excellent (me'ula) of the rooms, not 'upper storey'
it was an open (unroofed) upper storey, and they roofed it over
from 'behold now, I perceive that he is a holy man of God' (II Kings 4:9): a woman recognises [the character of] guests more than a man does
how she knew he was holy: she never saw a fly pass over his table
'he is holy' -- he is holy, but his attendant [Geichazi] is not holy
whoever hosts a Torah scholar in his home and lets him enjoy his property, Scripture credits him as if he offered the daily (tamid) offerings [the lemma: 'who passes by us tamid']
a person should not stand in a high place and pray
one who prays must align his feet [together] -- as it is said, 'and their feet were a straight foot' (Ezek 1:7)
'you shall not eat with the blood' (Lev 19:26) teaches: do not eat before you have prayed for your blood [your life]

whoever eats and drinks and afterwards prays, of him Scripture says 'and Me you have cast behind your back' (I Kings 14:9); the Holy One says: after this one has grown proud, he accepts on himself the kingdom of Heaven

R' Levi's account of Hezekiah's prayer: ומה שונמית שלא עשתה אלא קיר אחת קטנה החיית את בנה, אבי אבא שחפה את ההיכל כולו בכסף ובזהב על אחת כמה וכמה -- if the Shunamite's one small wall earned her son's revival, the Heichal covered in silver and gold earns all the more [Hezekiah's own]
R' Levi: 'wall' -- he spoke about matters of the wall (the Shunamite's wall against Solomon's Temple)
ומי לית ליה לחזקיהו החדש הזה לכם ראש חדשים -- זה ניסן ואין אחר ניסן?! how could Hezekiah have intercalated Nisan in Nisan, when the verse fixes Nisan as one month and no other?
'this month shall be for you the first of months' (Ex 12:2): this one is Nisan and no other is Nisan

אלא טעה בדשמואל -- he erred in Shmuel's rule: he intercalated on the thirtieth of Adar, which is fit to be Nisan; Shmuel forbids it for that reason, and Hezekiah held that 'since it is fit' is not said (= p_taah_bedishmuel)
rather, he erred in Shmuel's rule: what the baraita calls intercalating Nisan in Nisan was intercalating on the thirtieth of Adar, the day fit to be Nisan
R' Chanan: even if the master of dreams tells a man 'tomorrow you die', he should not hold himself back from [praying for] mercy
immediately: 'and Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the Lord' (Isa 38:2)
Reish Lakish: 'wall' -- [he prayed] from the chambers (kirot) of his heart
Rav (via Rav Yehuda): 'the good in Your eyes I did' -- that he joined redemption to prayer
the baraita: King Hezekiah did six things; on three they agreed with him and on three they did not
he hid away the Book of Remedies -- and they agreed with him
he stopped up the waters of Gichon -- and they did not agree with him
Rav Yehuda in Shmuel's name: the halakha follows R' Yehoshua
תניא נמי הכי -- the baraita that refuted version 1 corroborates version 2: the blessings are still said
version 2: 'he has not lost' means he has not lost the blessings -- they are still said
מדקתני כאדם הקורא בתורה -- מכלל דקורא בעונתה עדיף
R' Mani: greater is one who reads the Shema in its time than one who occupies himself with Torah
the mishnah: one who reads the Shema after its time has not lost, like a man reading in the Torah
version 1: reading after the time, one may no longer say the yotzer-or blessing -- what is lost is the blessings
the baraita: one who reads from here on has not lost -- but he DOES say two blessings before and one after
והיינו דרבי יהושע בן לוי: מאי דכתיב הנה לשלום מר לי מר -- the peace God sent Hezekiah was bitter to him because it came for David's sake, not his own
Hezekiah made [his request] depend on his own merit
whoever makes [his request] depend on his own merit -- they make it depend for him on others' merit
Moses made [his request] depend on others' merit
Beit Shammai: in the evening every person must recline and recite the Shema
Beit Hillel: every person recites the Shema as he is [in whatever position he happens to be]
the Torah's clause 'when you lie down and when you rise' (Deut 6:7)
narrative: R' Tarfon was once coming on the road and reclined to recite as Beit Shammai say, and endangered himself because of the bandits
the Sages to R' Tarfon: you deserved to forfeit your life, for you transgressed the words of Beit Hillel
